data.title: Cathie Wood Just Sold $7.7 Million of Amazon Stock
data.description:
Cathie Wood's ARK Invest funds sold 30,050 shares of Amazon on Thursday, Oct. 15, generating approximately $7.7 million based on the reported transaction value, as investors continue to assess the costs and potential returns of the company's artificial intelligence investments.

Amazon plans to spend about $220 billion on capital expenditures in 2026, with much of the investment directed toward AI infrastructure, data centers and related technology. The spending outlook has raised questions about how quickly these investments will translate into sustainable cash generation.

The company's latest quarterly results, however, showed continued operating growth. Revenue increased 20% year over year to $200.6 billion in the second quarter, while operating income rose 43% to $27.5 billion, according to its July 30 earnings release.

Amazon Web Services, the company's cloud computing division, delivered one of the strongest contributions. Revenue at AWS climbed 37% to $42.2 billion, marking its fastest growth in 18 quarters as demand for cloud and AI services expanded.

Despite the spending concerns, Wall Street remains positive on Amazon. ARK's sale alone does not establish a change in its broader investment view.

data.title: CBOT corn drops, down 1.1% in week, on dry Midwest harvest outlook
data.description:
Chicago Board of Trade corn futures fell for a fourth straight session on Friday, nearing a two-month low, on forecasts for dry weather over the coming week that should be favorable for continued harvesting of what is expected to be a massive US crop.

  • A recent stretch of dry weather around the US Midwest has allowed farmers to accelerate harvesting of summer crops, although many growers were gathering soybeans before corn. Rains slowed the pace of field work in the western Midwest at midweek, but a drier pattern was expected over the weekend and early next week, forecasters said.

  • The US Department of Agriculture reported net weekly export sales of US corn at 1,122,400 metric tons in the current marketing year for the week ended October 8, at the high end of a range of trade estimates.

  • CBOT December corn (CZ26) settled 3-3/4 cents lower at $4.74-1/4 a bushel after hitting overhead technical resistance at its 200-day moving average. The benchmark contract was down 1.1% in the week, its third straight weekly decline.

data.title: Bank of America Has Blunt Message on CoreWeave Stock After Selloff
data.description:
Bank of America is standing by CoreWeave after a sharp two-day selloff, arguing that the AI infrastructure company's growth outlook remains strong enough to justify a premium valuation despite mounting concerns over financing.

The bank kept its Buy rating and $140 price target on CoreWeave after the stock fell roughly 18% over two sessions.

Analyst Tal Liani said the decline likely reflected investor concerns around the increasingly difficult financing environment for AI infrastructure companies.

Still, BofA actually raised its revenue expectations.

The firm now forecasts CoreWeave revenue of $26.5 billion in 2027 and $43.3 billion in 2028, up from previous estimates of $26 billion and $41 billion.

That would represent growth of roughly 105% in 2027 and 63% in 2028.

BofA expects CoreWeave to add about 1.4 to 1.5 gigawatts of active power capacity annually over the next two years. Revenue per megawatt could also increase to around $14 by the end of 2028 from roughly $10 today as the company deploys Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin chips.

But the expansion comes at an enormous cost.

BofA raised its spending forecasts to $47.4 billion in 2027 and $49.8 billion in 2028.

The bank estimates CoreWeave could spend about $23.8 billion more cash than it generates in 2026 and another $24.8 billion in 2027.

Investor Takeaway

I think this call highlights the central contradiction in the CoreWeave story.

The company's growth outlook is extraordinary, but so are its financing requirements.

CoreWeave has at least $129 billion in contracted backlog, supported largely by major technology customers. Meta accounts for $35 billion and OpenAI another $22.4 billion, while Microsoft's share of backlog has fallen materially, improving customer diversification.

That backlog gives lenders visibility and may help CoreWeave finance expansion.

But investors still have to decide whether enough value remains for equity holders after the debt and capital spending required to build all that capacity.

For investors, the key things to watch are borrowing costs, free cash flow, power capacity additions, revenue per megawatt and whether the backlog continues translating into profitable growth.

BofA clearly believes the answer is yes. The market is becoming much less certain.

data.title: Nasdaq Posts Worst Weekly Drop in Months as Dow Edges to a Narrow Gain
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Stock Preachers  News Commentary - Wall Street closed a volatile week split sharply down the middle. The Dow finished Friday at 52,134.63, down 0.08% on the day but still up 0.93% for the week, while the Nasdaq Composite tumbled 1.28% Friday and 3.64% for the week, its worst stretch in months. The S&P 500 fell 1.43% weekly and the Russell 2000 dropped 2.43%. The VIX climbed to 17.02 and the VXN jumped to 22.89, underscoring the growing divide between mega-cap tech weakness and broader market resilience. Active Companies from around the markets with current developments this week include: Lockheed Martin (), Beretta Holding S.A. (), Truist Financial Corporation (), CLPS Incorporation (Nasdaq: CLPS), and Orvana Minerals Corp. ().

Friday's session showed the market's split personality in real time. The S&P 500 slid 0.58% to 7,699.50, pulling back from its week high of 7,821.67 and testing its 50-day EMA support near 7,681.97. The Nasdaq's 1.28% Friday drop capped a week that erased nearly 1,000 points, closing at 26,370.53 against a week high of 27,376.66, with RSI14 down to 40.4, signaling fading momentum.

Small caps lagged further, with the Russell 2000 down 1.03% Friday and 2.43% on the week, closing at 2,738.83 with an RSI14 of just 33.5, deep in weaker territory. The Dow bucked the trend, holding a 0.93% weekly gain and an 8.47% year-to-date advance, closing just under resistance at 52,281.19 and above its 50-day EMA support at 52,017.10.

Commodities sent mixed signals too. Gold slipped 0.10% for the week to $4,186.50 an ounce while silver fell 4.38% to $57.51. WTI crude jumped 4.17% weekly to $97.65 a barrel, up 70.06% year-to-date, while the 10-year Treasury yield eased 13 basis points to 5.11%, even as it ticked up 2 basis points on the day.

The full report breaks down the key support and resistance levels traders are watching next week along with sector-by-sector sentiment across the divided market.

CONTINUED... Read this and more news at: https://stockpreachers.com/articles/a-week-that-split-the-market-right-down-the-middle/

In other industry developments and happenings in the market this week include:

Lockheed Martin () Lockheed Martin delivered a C-130J-30 Super Hercules aircraft to the U.S. Navy at its Marietta, Georgia facility on Oct. 15, marking the start of its transformation into the E-130J Phoenix II, the Navy's next-generation TACAMO mission platform for airborne nuclear command and control.

The aircraft will next be transferred to Northrop Grumman, the mission systems integrator, to complete the conversion. "This delivery marks a historic milestone for the U.S. Navy, Lockheed Martin, and the nation's strategic communications network," said Trish Pagan, vice president of Lockheed Martin's Air Mobility & Maritime Missions.

The delivery revives the link between the TACAMO mission and the Hercules family, which previously flew the mission via the EC-130Q variant from 1963 until 1993.

Beretta Holding S.A. () Beretta Holding announced preliminary results of its cash tender offer for shares of Sturm, Ruger & Company at $44.80 per share. The offer, which expired Oct. 15, sought up to 2,400,184 shares but drew 3,589,647 shares validly tendered, excluding 2,652,256 shares tendered by notice of guaranteed delivery.

Because the offer was oversubscribed, Beretta Holding estimates a preliminary proration factor of approximately 38.45%, subject to confirmation by the depositary following the guaranteed delivery period.

"This investment represents a significant milestone for Beretta Holding. It marks our first participation in a publicly listed company and opens a new chapter in our development as a long-term investor in the U.S. capital markets," said Pietro Gussalli Beretta, Chairman and CEO of Beretta Holding.

Truist Financial Corporation () Truist Financial Corporation reported its third quarter 2026 results, with details available through its earnings release, investor presentation and Quarterly Performance Summary posted to the company's investor relations website.

The company hosted a live earnings call at 8 a.m. ET the same day, with a replay made available on its website for 30 days.

Truist describes itself as a top-10 commercial bank with total assets of $554 billion as of Sept. 30, 2026, offering consumer and small business banking, commercial and corporate banking, investment banking, wealth management, payments and specialized lending.

CLPS Incorporation (Nasdaq: CLPS) CLPS Incorporation reported full fiscal year 2026 revenue growth of 4.7% year-over-year to $172.2 million, and second-half revenue growth of 6.6% to $87.1 million, despite revenue pressure from the downsizing of a key client's China Solution Centers.

Revenue from customized IT solution services surged 113.9% year-over-year to $5.9 million for the full year, while revenue generated outside mainland China rose 47.5% to $62.7 million, with Hong Kong SAR up 61.0% to $23.2 million and Japan up 122.7% to $4.5 million.

"Fiscal 2026 was a pivotal year of structural transition and resilience for CLPS," said Raymond Lin, Chief Executive Officer of CLPS. "Since becoming a publicly traded company in 2018, we have expanded our topline from $48.9 million to $172.2 million, delivering a robust 17.0% compound annual growth rate over the past eight years."

Orvana Minerals Corp. () Orvana Minerals Corp. reported fourth quarter and fiscal 2026 production results, with consolidated FY2026 production of 45,160 gold equivalent ounces, comprised of 39,282 gold ounces, 3.1 million pounds of copper and 112,499 silver ounces.

Orovalle produced 37,775 ounces of gold and 2.9 million pounds of copper in FY2026, exceeding gold production guidance of 34,000 to 37,000 ounces and landing within copper guidance of 2,700 to 3,000 thousand pounds. EMIPA produced its first dore and copper cathodes from the expanded Don Mario Plant during the quarter but came in below the company's FY2026 guidance, which was withdrawn on September 17, 2026.

"Looking ahead to FY2027, our focus remains on sustaining disciplined production performance and operational efficiency while managing inflationary cost pressures arising from broader global conditions and continued workforce challenges."

data.title: Air Canada Adds Direct Flights to U.S. Cities Amid Gradual Travel Rebound — Market Talk
data.description: Air Canada is expanding its routes to the U.S. as part of its partnership with United Airlines as more Canadians travel south. Under the renewed Trans-border Joint Business Agreement, which supports more than 1,200 connecting itineraries and continued network growth between the two countries, Air Canada will launch several new nonstop routes starting next summer including service connecting Toronto to Louisville, Montreal to Indianapolis, and Edmonton to Newark. The expansion coincides with a sustained recovery in cross-border travel following a sharp dip in 2025. In September, roughly 1.9 million Canadians returned from trips to the U.S., up 6.8% from a year prior, according to Statistics Canada. That followed a summer peak in July, when Canadian trips to the U.S. reached 2.8 million, a 10.1% year-over-year increase. (adriano.marchese@wsj.com)

data.title: From Verizon to UnitedHealth, Corporate America Is Balking at 'Tokenized' Stocks — WSJ
data.description:
By Vicky Ge Huang

The country's top securities regulator made a push last month to bring tokenized stock trading to the U.S. Now, corporate America is pushing back.

AI chip maker Broadcom, telecom stalwart Verizon Communications and UnitedHealth are among the companies objecting to the Securities and Exchange Commission's plan for tokenizing their stocks, according to a regulatory filing.

Many exchanges and trading venues are eager to offer digital tokens that represent traditional shares and can trade 24/7. The goal is to appeal to a class of new-age investors who have grown up on crypto and want to trade round-the-clock. But some companies worry the SEC's plan for tokenization might create a shadow stock market, distort trading and confuse investors.

And even Nasdaq, which is developing its own tokenization platform, has said it would opt out of having its own shares tokenized under the framework proposed by the SEC. In an FAQ on its website, the exchange operator cited concerns that the plan could create a parallel market outside the National Market System, a series of rules that bind U.S. stock exchanges and help ensure investors get the best available prices on trades on any platform.

"We have determined that our shares should not trade on a venue that does not display best prices in real time, report to the consolidated tape, or provide the transparency investors expect," said a Nasdaq spokesperson, adding that the exchange remains committed to tokenization.

Some Wall Street players warn that the new framework creates hidden risks for public companies. Notices sent by tokenized trading platforms to corporate emails or postal addresses are potentially not actively monitored, and failing to respond within 30 days is treated as tacit consent. Moreover, the framework offers no blanket opt-out, meaning companies will have to monitor and object to every trading venue individually.

The SEC's order last month temporarily exempts authorized trading venues and market makers from certain rules that previously prevented trading in digital tokens that represent shares of listed companies.

But it comes with some safeguards: The tokens permitted by the SEC exemptions will carry the same shareholder rights granted to investors in traditional stocks, including dividend payouts and proxy votes. And before a tokenized securities venue can begin trading any stock, it must give the issuing company 30 days notice. If the company objects, the venue can't proceed with the offering.

The 30-day decision window is rapidly closing for many corporate issuers. OKXICE, a 50-50 joint venture between New York Stock Exchange owner Intercontinental Exchange and crypto exchange OKX, triggered the clock last week when it became one of the first entities to notify regulators of their plans to launch a tokenized stock-trading platform under the SEC's framework.

Nine companies needed little time to make up their mind. In addition to Broadcom, Verizon and UnitedHealth, Cerebras Systems, AppLovin, Applied Digital, Rocket Lab, CoreWeave and Applied Optoelectronics have each opted out.

A spokeswoman for Applied Optoelectronics said the fiber-optic manufacturer objected because it wasn't sure how tokenization would affect its stock price, liquidity and volatility.

"We are also mindful of the risk of investor confusion about AOI's involvement in the offering, which we did not sponsor or endorse," she said. "At this stage, we don't see a clear benefit to AOI or our shareholders that justifies these uncertainties."

OKXICE said it still plans to launch trading for dozens of U.S.-listed companies on X Layer, a blockchain developed by OKX, including Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Tesla, JPMorgan Chase and Walmart.

Andrew Cuomo, the co-chair of OKXICE, has said that he expects some companies to be skeptical and exercise caution about tokenizing their stocks and that is to be expected for any major change. "It is the first step toward tokenizing securities," Cuomo, the former governor of New York, said in a recent interview with The Journal.

Market maker Citadel Securities said in a letter to the SEC last year that the exemptions could facilitate the "emergence of a 'shadow' U.S. equity market" and "allow tokenized U.S. equities to trade completely outside of the national market system." The firm argued that bypassing traditional exchange rules could fragment liquidity, or scatter trading activity across different platforms, and undermine investor protections.

Nasdaq echoed this point, arguing this shadow market "can become disconnected from the broader market in both pricing and price transparency."

Their worries aren't unfounded. Overseas, synthetic tokens, which track stock prices without conferring ownership rights, sometimes deviated significantly from real stock values during off hours and periods of low trading volume. Critics warn that similar risks could emerge under the SEC's framework, including price tracking errors, confusion around proxy voting and dividend distributions as well as legal liabilities for corporate issuers if individual investors suffer big losses in tokens that trade wildly different from the underlying stocks.

Earlier this year, the SEC approved Nasdaq's proposal to allow the trading of some stocks and exchange-traded products in tokenized forms. The exchange took part in a trial run to tokenize securities that Wall Street firms keep at Depository Trust & Clearing, a leading trade processor. It is also working with crypto exchange Kraken and issuing companies in developing its plan to offer tokenized stocks on its exchange.

Brett Redfearn, president of tokenization firm Securitize, said some corporate issuers could object to being listed on one tokenized trading venue without rejecting tokenization altogether. Securitize recently rolled out tokenized stock trading for U.S. investors and the stocks it tokenizes are expected to trade on OKXICE's platform.

Some lawyers note that the SEC's innovation exemptions are a limited experiment to gather information, not a commitment to using this framework permanently. Rodrigo Seira, a partner at law firm Cooley, said the firm has spoken with the agency a couple of times and expects revisions to the current innovation exemptions.

"Part of what they're doing with this exemptive order is trying to get as much information as they can so that they can inform their ultimate rules and make them better, and also make them more defensible from a potential administrative challenge," Seira said.

Write to Vicky Ge Huang at vicky.huang@wsj.com

data.title: Yields on Treasurys, European Government Bonds Edge Higher — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Emese Bartha and Jessica Fleetham

Yields on U.S. Treasurys and European government bonds edged higher on Friday, pulling away from the multiweek lows reached the previous day.

That advance still left yields below the multidecades highs reached last week. Investors have turned their attention away from concerns about inflation and risks of higher interest rates. Now their focus is on the economic impact of high borrowing costs and the sustainability of debt-funded AI investments.

The 10-year Treasury yield traded at 5.123%, up from an intraday low of 5.068%.

Markets priced in 83% odds of an interest rate hold by the Federal Reserve at its Oct. 28 meeting, up from 72% on Thursday, according to CME, following Chairman Kevin Warsh's remarks during an International Monetary Fund event in Bangkok. Warsh stopped short of giving forward guidance, after officials have indicated in recent days that there is no hurry to hike.

U.S. industrial production rose 0.7% in September after an upwardly revised increase of 0.1% in August. Analysts polled by The Wall Street Journal expected a 0.4% increase last month.

The 10-year German Bund yield was at 3.453%, having hit a five-week low of 3.352% on Thursday.

Bond markets face a "rollercoaster ride" of "one step forward, one step back," pulled by changes in oil prices and risk sentiment, Commerzbank rates strategists said in a note.

Since bond yields globally hit multiyear highs earlier this month, investors have been tempted back into buying government bonds again, particularly given concerns about the sustainability of the AI trade.

"U.S. Treasury yields may have reached levels where their elevated levels weigh on risk sentiment," said Jussi Hiljanen, chief rates strategist at SEB.

Investors are also starting to question whether interest rates will rise as much as markets are currently anticipating. Money markets currently price in up to three rate increases by the Federal Reserve and European Central Bank over the next year, and four by the Bank of England, LSEG data showed.

U.S. rates markets are grappling with two key questions--whether the market is pricing in too many interest-rate hikes over the next year and whether bond yields have peaked, Societe Generale rates strategists said in a note.

The risk of energy prices staying elevated and keeping inflation high remains a concern for bond investors, however.

Inflation remains the pivotal variable for markets because it will influence both the direction of monetary policy and the path of government bond yields, said Laura Lake and Tim Crawmer, senior strategists at Payden & Rygel, in a note.

"If inflation cools more decisively, bonds could deliver price appreciation in addition to income," they said.

Oil prices rose on Friday, with front-month Brent crude up 3% at $109.

  • Paulo Trevisani contributed to this article.

Write to Emese Bartha at emese.bartha@wsj.com and Jessica Fleetham at jessica.fleetham@wsj.com

data.title: Wall Street tumbles as worries about AI trade and high oil prices weigh
data.description:
Key points:
  • Chips, AI infrastructure companies fall as debt concerns linger
  • S&P 500 and Nasdaq head for steep weekly losses
  • S&P 500 -1.22%, Nasdaq -2.19%, Dow -0.55%

By Noel Randewich and Purvi Agarwal

Wall Street tumbled on Friday, with CoreWeave, Broadcom and other AI-related technology stocks under renewed pressure, while a jump in oil prices spooked traders heading into the weekend.

The Nasdaq was on track for a loss of over 4% for the week, hammered by concerns that debt-laden AI infrastructure companies may not turn profits in time to repay debts, particularly with borrowing costs expected to rise.

Nvidia-backed CoreWeave slumped 12%, bringing its loss over the past five sessions to about 25%. The data center operator's bonds also sold off sharply this week, pushing yields above 15%.

Broadcom fell 3.6%, and the PHLX chip index sank 2.5%, on track for its eighth straight day of declines.

Investors on Friday were also watching oil prices jump more than 3% due to Middle East supply worries.

"There is some fear in the market," said Rob Haworth, senior investment strategist at U.S. Bank Wealth Management in ​Seattle. "High oil prices, in particular, tend to weigh on the price/earnings multiple of stocks, and so I think you have investors looking to be cautious into the weekend rather than take more risk."

Adding to concerns around AI financing, some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors are weighing a lower valuation for the company in its upcoming IPO, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The S&P 500 was down 1.22% at 7,649.71 points.

The Nasdaq declined 2.19% to 26,128.13 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 0.55% at 51,891.77 points.

Six of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes declined, led lower by communication services , down 2.52%, followed by a 2.38% loss in information technology .

The S&P 500 was set for its steepest weekly loss since January, and the Nasdaq was heading for its sharpest weekly fall since June.

Third-quarter earnings season shifts into gear next week with reports from Tesla , Meta Platforms and Procter & Gamble . Analysts on average see quarterly earnings surging over 30%, driven by AI-related megacaps, according to LSEG data.

While the S&P 500 remains up about 12% in 2025, most of that gain has come from AI-related tech stocks, and the index’s median component has climbed only about 6%, year to date. About 185 S&P 500 stocks have lost ground in 2025.

Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer inflation reports this week showed price pressures were extending beyond energy commodities.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh on Friday voiced optimism about US economic strength and surprise about how well global economies have been "hanging in there" during a lingering energy shock and tighter monetary policy to fight inflation.

Markets increasingly expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged this month. Barclays now expects 25-basis-point hikes each in December and January.

Tesla dropped 2.5% after the electric-vehicle maker unveiled a redesigned Roadster, powered by rocket-style thrusters, developed in collaboration with SpaceX.

Netflix appointed former Disney executive Peter Rice as chief content officer on Thursday. Its shares were down 2.9%.

Declining stocks outnumbered rising ones within the S&P 500 (.AD.SPX) by a 1.3-to-one ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 19 new highs and one new low; the Nasdaq recorded 49 new highs and 263 new lows.

data.title: Minnesota Records 42 Measles Cases In 2026 As Outbreak Spreads
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - The Minnesota Department of Health said the measles outbreak in Fillmore County, in southeastern Minnesota, has grown to six cases, doubling since the beginning of the month.

The update comes as the state deals with two separate measles outbreaks that began in mid-September in rural Fillmore and Todd counties.

Minnesota has recorded 42 measles cases so far in 2026, already exceeding the 26 cases reported in 2025. In 2024, the state recorded 70 cases, most of which affected unvaccinated Somali American children in the Twin Cities.

'Given how contagious measles is, the case count will very likely grow in the days and weeks ahead,' the health department stated.

According to the health department, all people infected in the recent outbreaks were unvaccinated.

Children in Minnesota are required to receive two doses of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine before entering kindergarten, unless their families obtain an exemption.

However, the number of kindergartners whose families have claimed non-medical exemptions from vaccination has increased sharply since 2020, reflecting growing concerns about vaccines.

During the 2025-2026 school year, 6.8% of kindergartners in Minnesota had non-medical exemptions, compared with the national average of 4%, according to data from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Nationwide, the U.S. has recorded more than 4,000 confirmed measles cases so far in 2026.

data.title: Ambarella may be seeing interest from a third bidder - report
data.description:
Ambarella is speculated to have garnered interest from a third bidder.

There's speculation that one of the world's biggest AI chipmakers has entered a sales process for Ambarella , according to traders who cited a Betaville “uncooked” alert that was circulating on Friday.

The bidding war now consists of the unidentified chipmaker, NXP Semiconductors , and Qualcomm . Betaville last Friday said Qualcomm is speculated to be working with banks on a potential deal. The third bidder is described as bigger than NXPI and QCOM combined.

There's some speculation that the sales process is in its late stages and a deal could be announced in the coming weeks, according to Betaville.

Betaville first reported about Ambarella () takeover speculation in late July. Ambarella jumped 16% on July 31 following the FT report that NXP Semiconductors () was in talks to acquire the chip designer.

Shares of Ambarella pared much of an earlier decline on Friday.

Florence Tresarrieu, President, and Chief Executive Officer, and Juan Alonso, Vice-President and Chief Financial Officer will host a conference call for the investment community on, Friday, November 13, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. (ET).

To access the conference call, please dial 1-437-900-0527 or toll-free 1-888-510-2154. You can also join via webcast here: https://app.webinar.net/ZVQgJeQJ8e5.

About Corby Spirit and Wine Limited

Corby is a leading Canadian manufacturer, marketer and distributor of spirits, imported wines and ready-to-drink beverages. Corby's portfolio of owned-brands includes some of the most renowned brands in Canada, including J.P. Wiser's®, Lot 40®, and Pike Creek® Canadian whiskies, Polar Ice® vodka, and McGuinness® liqueurs, Ungava® gin, Cabot Trail® maple-based liqueurs, Chic Choc® spiced rum, Cottage Springs® and Nude® ready-to-drink beverages and Foreign Affair® wines. data.title: Gold set for a weekly drop as traders assess Fed signals
data.description:
Key points:
  • Fed's Warsh mum on rate-path view
  • US PPI and CPI data come in hotter than expected
  • Silver, platinum and palladium head for weekly losses

By Pablo Sinha

Gold prices were largely steady on Friday and were on track for a weekly loss as traders weighed the prospect of further Federal Reserve rate hikes this year following a run of hotter-than-expected US inflation data.

Spot gold was down 0.1% at $4,165.12 per ounce by 02:07 p.m. EDT (1807 GMT) but was down 0.7% so far in the week.

US gold futures for December delivery settled 0.3% higher at $4,181.10 per ounce.

"We're very much rangebound and tilting toward the lower bound of support, the main reason being we still have a lot of ambiguity in what the Fed will do," Bart Melek, global head of commodity strategy at TD Securities, said.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh voiced optimism about US economic strength but gave no clues about the central bank's rate-path trajectory.

Data on Thursday showed US producer prices increased by the most in 4-1/2 years last month. The data followed Wednesday's consumer price report, which showed prices accelerated in September.

Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said the data was "discouraging" while Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said the Fed might need to hike interest rates more aggressively if there were to be a notable deterioration in the public's inflation expectations.

Traders largely expect the US central bank to hold rates steady this month, while pricing in a 90% chance of a rate hike in December, according to the CME's FedWatch Tool.

Although gold is typically seen as an inflation hedge, higher interest rates tend to reduce the appeal of the non-yielding metal.

"Over the rest of this year, gold prices are likely to edge lower as the Fed continues raising rates and fears around the end of the AI boom prove to be temporary," Hamad Hussain, a climate and commodities economist at Capital Economics, said.

Elsewhere, gold traded at a premium in India this week for the first time in more than three months as a pullback in prices boosted jewellery purchases.

Among other metals, spot silver fell 0.7% to $57.05 per ounce, platinum was unchanged at $1,626.15 and palladium was down 1.1% to $1,113.61. All three metals headed for weekly losses.

data.title: Victoria's Secret is still in the early innings of a multi-year turnaround - Needham
data.description:
Needham started off coverage on Victoria's Secret with a Buy rating on its view that the retailer is only in the early innings of a multi-year turnaround.

Analyst Tom Nikic pointed to improvements to the Victoria's Secret management team, product assortment, and the marketing upside. Notably, Nikic and his team think the VSXY's EPS can double over the next five years.

As for the near term, strong quarter-to-date channel checks and lower promotions have Nikic calling Victoria's Secret a compelling beat-and-raise story.

Looking ahead, the company is seen as being a beneficiary of increased adoption of GLP-1 weight loss medicines as slimmed-down women shop for new clothes. All in, we view this as a compelling momentum name heading into 2027

Needham assigned a price target of $106 on VSXY based on a 16X multiple to its FY28 EPS estimate. The PT assumes mid-single-digit revenue growth the next two years and EBIT margin expansion.

Shares of VSXY are up more than 60% on a year-to-date basis, but the Seeking Alpha Quant Rating is still flashing Strong Buy.

data.title: Tech Stocks Slump as Nasdaq Faces Weekly Loss — WSJ
data.description:
By Chelsey Dulaney

Tech stocks are poised to finish a tough week on a down note as chip and AI-related shares come under new pressure.

The Nasdaq composite is down 2% in afternoon trading, which would leave the tech-heavy benchmark with a loss of more than 4% for the week, its sharpest since June. The S&P 500 is down about 1% Friday, while the Dow industrials are lower by 0.5% but still up for the week.

The AI trade remains on fragile footing, with CoreWeave shares coming under renewed pressure today. The Nvidia-backed compute provider has been at the center of this week's tech rout, as investors fret over how higher borrowing costs will hit the most highly leveraged players in the data-center buildout.

Markets had been steadying earlier, while investors pared bets that the Fed will raise interest rates this month after comments from Chairman Kevin Warsh.

Speaking overnight in Bangkok, Warsh did little to dispel investors' view that the Fed isn't in a rush to raise rates despite a string of hotter-than-expected inflation readings this week.

The dollar retreated along with rate-hike expectations. Benchmark 10-year Treasurys are flirting with their best week since February

Brent crude prices are up about 3% to $109 a barrel.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Elon Musk Pours a Fortune Into Saving Texas for Republicans - Update
data.description:
By Sabrina Rodriguez and Anthony DeBarros

Elon Musk is putting a small fortune into Republicans' effort to salvage the Senate seat in Texas, seen as critical to the party keeping control of the chamber in the fall elections.

According to federal filings, Musk donated $158 million to Senate Republicans' super PAC in September — the same amount that was immediately funneled to a group backing Republican Ken Paxton's Senate bid.

The new disclosures show that Musk, the world's richest person, is behind much of the money that has been pumped into the Texas Senate race to help keep Paxton financially competitive as his Democratic opponent James Talarico has significantly outraised him throughout the race.

Musk is a Texas resident and has several companies, including Tesla and SpaceX, based in the Lone Star State.

In September, Musk sent two large donations to the Senate Leadership Fund, Senate Republicans' main super PAC.

On Sept. 9, the first day of the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, Musk funneled $75 million to SLF. The following day, the super PAC moved $75 million into a connected entity named Texas PAC. Two weeks later, Musk gave $83 million to SLF — and again, the following day, the group sent the same amount to Texas PAC, which is the biggest advertiser in the Texas contest, according to AdImpact data.

And in August, he also gave $10 million to Lone Star Liberty PAC, a super PAC boosting Paxton.

Overall, Musk gave more than $250 million to Republican-aligned groups in the third quarter, campaign-finance filings show. Among that was $89 million he gave to his own America PAC.

"If Democrats take control of Washington and win key gubernatorial and attorney-general races this November, then America risks becoming a socialist, woke and borderless country," said Andrew Romeo, a spokesman for America PAC. He said the Musk donations are designed to give Republicans "a fighting chance to defy history."

Cristóbal Alex, a Democratic strategist, said Musk "has spent billions trying to get to Mars, but apparently the real moonshot is a Senate seat" for Paxton, pointing to Paxton's various legal and ethical scandals.

Musk launched America PAC to support Trump's 2024 election, and the group now backs Republicans in competitive races across the country, spending over $23 million since July to back individual candidates.

The GOP has a 53-47 majority in the Senate. Democrats are feeling increasingly bullish about their chances of flipping the Senate, in part because of their strong showing so far in Texas.

Talarico has consistently held a narrow lead in polls, raising Democrats' hopes that they could win statewide office in Texas for the first time since 1994. Such hopes for the party have repeatedly fallen short, most notably when former Rep. Beto O'Rourke narrowly lost to Sen. Ted Cruz in 2018.

The matchup between Paxton, the state attorney general, and Talarico, a state lawmaker, is one of the most expensive races this election cycle. And Republicans are significantly outspending Democrats in the final stretch of the race.

For the individual campaigns, Talarico raised $64 million in the third quarter this year, his campaign said — more than three times the over $18 million Paxton reported in the same quarter.

Going into the midterms, Republicans had a money advantage over Democrats. They have been throwing hundreds of millions of dollars into races across the country. Still, polls haven't shown significant shifts in high-profile contests since more money started pumping in.

data.title: Sanyasi Ayurveda sells 0.53% stake in PC Jeweller
data.description:
Sanyasi Ayurveda has offloaded a 0.53 percent stake in jewellery retailer PC Jeweller through open-market transactions on October 16.

Despite the stake sale, PC Jeweller extended its rally for a second consecutive session, gaining 9.93 percent to close at Rs 16.28, its highest closing level in three months.

Sanyasi Ayurveda sold 5.17 crore equity shares, representing 0.53 percent of PC Jeweller's paid-up equity capital, for Rs 84.2 crore. The sale was part of its 1.84 percent stake, equivalent to 18.04 crore shares, held in the company as of September 2026.

The shares were sold at Rs 16.28 apiece.

In the previous session, investor Aditya Kumar Halwasiya acquired a 0.52 percent stake in the jewellery retailer for Rs 73.59 crore.

Meanwhile, the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA), owned by the Government of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, acquired 1.73 lakh equity shares in Natco Pharma at Rs 25.51 per share on rights basis.

Natco Pharma opened its 1.7-crore-share rights issue, worth Rs 1,279.4 crore, on October 12. The issue will close on October 22. The issue price has been fixed at Rs 750 per share.

Activity was also seen in Quanto Agroworld, where Capacious Wealth Management LLP acquired one lakh shares from Vikasa India EIF I Fund – Share Class P at Rs 62 per share.

data.description:

Rath AG // Rath Group reaches agreement with its key financial creditors on the terms of a transformation agreement and launches a transformation programme

16-Oct-2026 / 20:08 CET/CEST

Disclosure of an inside information acc. to Article 17 MAR of the Regulation (EU) No 596/2014, transmitted by EQS News - a service of EQS Group.

The issuer is solely responsible for the content of this announcement.

Rath Aktiengesellschaft // Rath Group reaches agreement with its key financial creditors on the terms of a transformation agreement and launches a transformation programme involving the closure and relocation of production sites Vienna, 16th October 2026. Rath Aktiengesellschaft and four of its subsidiaries have reached agreement with their key financial creditors on the terms of an agreement governing a transformation process. The agreement provides for the adjustment and extension of the existing financing arrangements until 31 December 2029. The financing arrangements will be subject to higher interest rates and fees and the provision of extensive collateral. The parties have agreed, in principle, to suspend ongoing principal repayments until 31 December 2029, with any early repayments to be made, where applicable, from excess liquidity and extraordinary cash inflows. The agreement also provides for a waiver of dividend distributions. As part of the Rath Group's transformation process, its European production network is to be reorganised by 31 December 2028. The production site in Meißen, Germany, will be discontinued, and production will be relocated to the existing sites in Krummnußbaum, Austria, and Owensville, USA. Employees at the Meißen site will be offered continued employment at the Bennewitz site in Germany. The production site in Budapest, Hungary, will be closed by 31 December 2028. Most of the production capacity currently located there will be transferred to the sites in Krummnußbaum and Bennewitz. The measures are intended to increase efficiency and improve the Group's cost structure.
